summary: Rudolf Meringer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin under Johannes Schmidt. He held posts at Vienna before serving as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Graz (1899–1930).
Rudolf Much was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna from around 1883 to 1887 and later held a post there from around 1906 to 1934.

Rudolf Otto was a religious studies scholar, philosopher, and Indologist who studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Göttingen, and Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. He held theology and professorial posts at Göttingen (1897–1914), Breslau (1914–1917), and Marburg (1917–1929).

Rudolf Otto Franke worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Bonn and Göttingen under August Fick and Franz Kielhorn, later serving as Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin (1890) and professor at Königsberg (1895–1927).
Rudolf Seydel was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig from around 1852 to 1856 and held a post there from around 1860 to 1892.

Rudolf Steiner worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at TU Wien (~1879–1883) and the University of Rostock (~1891), and held a post at the Goethe and Schiller Archives from around 1890 to 1896.

Rudolf Stübe was a religious studies scholar. Between 1890 and 1894, he studied at the University of Rostock, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel, and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Rudolf Thomas Siegfried worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and in Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, later serving as Lecturer in Sanskrit at Trinity College Dublin (1858–1862).

Rudolf Thurneysen was a linguist who studied at Basel, Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, Berlin under Heinrich Zimmer, and Paris under Henri Gaidoz. He held posts at Jena (1882–1887), Freiburg (1887–1913), and Bonn (1913–1923).

Rudolf Westphal was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Marburg and Tübingen under Johann Gildemeister. He held posts at Tübingen (~1852–1855), Breslau (1857–1862), Fellin, Goldingen, and the Katkov Lyceum (1875–1881).

Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Tübinger Stift under Heinrich Ewald and under Eugène Burnouf, and spent his career at the University of Tübingen as Privatdozent (1845) and Extraordinarius (1848–1895).

Rudolph Rahmann studied at Missionshaus St. Gabriel and the University of Vienna under Wilhelm Schmidt and Wilhelm Koppers. He held posts at Fu Jen Catholic University, University of San Carlos, and University of Fribourg (1956–1960).

Rudrapatna Shamasastry worked in Indology, history, and archaeology, studying at Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, University of Madras, Oriental University, and University of Calcutta. He served as Principal of Sri Chamarajendra Samskrita Maha Patashala, Curator at Mysore ORI, and Director of Mysore Archaeological Department.

Ruixuan Chen works in Buddhist, Indological, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Chen studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann, Adelheid Mette, Olav Hackstein, Helmut Tauscher, and Paul Harrison at Leiden University, and is a faculty member at Peking University.

Rulon Wells was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (~1935–1939) and Harvard University (~1939–1942), and held a long-term post at Yale University (~1945–1989).
Rune Edvin Arvid Johansson was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon and Lund University, where he also served as a lecturer.

Rupert Gethin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his BA and PhD at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins, subsequently holding positions at the University of Bristol from 1987, Pali Text Society, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Ruriko Sakuma works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Having studied at Nagoya University, she has held posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Chicago and under D. T. Suzuki, Sokei-an, Zuigan Goto, and Mukai Kono. She was director of the First Zen Institute and abbess of Ryōsen-an.

Ruth Gamble works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at RMIT and the Australian National University, and held posts at the University of Munich, the Australian National University, and La Trobe University.
